description: Implement two-factor authentication using TOTP (Time-based One-Time Password) via pragmarx/google2fa-laravel package. QR code setup page, recovery codes, 2FA challenge at login, required for admins, optional for other roles.
steps: Add pragmarx/google2fa-laravel package to composer.json: 'composer require pragmarx/google2fa-laravel'

Create migration adding 2FA columns to users table: two_factor_secret (text, nullable, encrypted), two_factor_recovery_codes (text, nullable, encrypted JSON array), two_factor_enabled (boolean, default false), two_factor_enabled_at (timestamp, nullable)

Create app/Services/TwoFactorService.php with methods: generateSecret(), generateQrCodeUrl(User), generateRecoveryCodes(), verifyCode(User, code), verifyRecoveryCode(User, code), enableTwoFactor(User), disableTwoFactor(User)

Create app/Http/Controllers/Settings/TwoFactorController.php with methods: show() for 2FA setup page, enable() to activate 2FA with QR code and recovery codes, disable() to turn off 2FA, verify() to confirm 2FA code during setup

Create resources/views/settings/two-factor.blade.php following Mwalimu design with: QR code display (using google2fa's inline SVG QR), manual secret key entry option, recovery codes display (16 codes, 8 chars each, one-time use), enable/disable toggle
Create app/Http/Middleware/TwoFactorChallengeMiddleware.php that intercepts login for 2FA-enabled users and redirects to 2FA challenge page before reaching dashboard
Create app/Http/Controllers/Auth/TwoFactorChallengeController.php with show() for challenge page and verify() for code submission
Create resources/views/auth/two-factor-challenge.blade.php following login.blade.php design with 6-digit code input and 'Use recovery code instead' link
Update LoginController.php: after successful Auth::attempt(), check if user has 2FA enabled - if yes, store user ID in session and redirect to 2FA challenge instead of dashboard
In TwoFactorChallengeController->verify(), validate TOTP code using TwoFactorService, complete login with Auth::login(), clear 2FA session data, and redirect to dashboard

Add middleware to routes/web.php ensuring admins must have 2FA enabled: create TwoFactorRequired middleware that checks auth()->user()->isAdmin() && !auth()->user()->two_factor_enabled and redirects to 2FA setup with warning
Add routes: GET/POST /settings/two-factor, POST /settings/two-factor/enable, POST /settings/two-factor/disable, GET/POST /auth/two-factor-challenge
Add '2FA Security' link to settings navigation
Test complete flow: enable 2FA as student (optional), enable 2FA as admin (required), log out, log in and complete 2FA challenge, test recovery code, disable 2FA
acceptance_criteria: Users can enable 2FA from settings page with QR code and recovery codes
Admins are required to enable 2FA and cannot access platform without it
Other roles (tutor, student, parent) can optionally enable 2FA
After login, 2FA-enabled users must enter 6-digit TOTP code from authenticator app
Recovery codes work as fallback when authenticator app unavailable
2FA can be disabled by entering current TOTP code for verification
QR code works with Google Authenticator, Authy, 1Password, etc.
All 2FA pages match Mwalimu brand design
verification: Log in as student at http://localhost:8000/login
Click 'Enable 2FA' - verify QR code and recovery codes displayed
Scan QR code with Google Authenticator app on phone
Enter 6-digit code from app and submit - verify 2FA enabled success message
Log out and log in again - verify redirect to 2FA challenge page after password entry
Enter code from authenticator app - verify successful login to dashboard
Log out again, log in, and try recovery code instead - verify it works and code is consumed
Navigate to 2FA settings and disable 2FA - verify requires TOTP code to disable
Log in as admin user - verify redirect to 2FA setup if not enabled
Verify admin cannot access any admin routes without enabling 2FA
Check storage/logs/laravel.log for any errors during flow
